**Pathway-resolved decoherence in non-Abelian anyonic systems**

Decoherence in anyonic media is usually reported as a single storage time, obscuring distinct mechanisms that attack encoded information at different protocol stages. For a non-Abelian anyonic system with fixed total topological charge under weak static Markovian coupling, decoherence resolves into three identifiable pathways: fusion-channel dephasing (P1) via gapless edge modes, charge-sector leakage (P2) via quasiparticle poisoning, and readout backaction (P3) from an incomplete measurement record. The three are pairwise discriminable — P1 decays visibility with stationary populations, P2 produces telegraph-like phase jumps, P3 responds to record retention. Evaluating rates for Ising-type devices with realistic bulk-edge coupling yields a crossover depth ~1 μm at 25 mK, beyond which a device is leakage-limited rather than dephasing-limited. Conditioning interferometric readout on the retained record recovers fidelity 0.91 against 0.58 unconditioned, the gap attributable to P3 alone. The classification assumes static Markovian environments; driven or structured baths are outside its scope. Joint work with M. Reyes (Stanmore University).
